title: Which button takes the lift from floor negative two to negative one?
description: The lift stands one floor below the ground floor and must reach the floor just above it, both under the ground. The movement is the target floor take away the starting floor, and the lift shaft shows the answer. Keeko's doubt is that two negative signs make the button negative.
teaching_notes: One idea: the movement needed is target floor take away starting floor, even when both floors are below the ground. Watch for students who see two negative signs and press a negative button, though the target floor is higher.

source: If the Target Floor is −1 and Starting Floor is −2, what but
video_script.why: The child finds the button press when both floors are below the ground.
video_script.substitution: Use the book's own floors: starting floor negative two and target floor negative one.
video_script.anchor: the lift in {{NAME_10}} below the ground floor, from floor negative two to floor negative one
video_script.wrong_move: sees the negative signs on both floors and gives a negative button, though the target floor is higher
video_script.payoff_line: The button press is positive one.

names.{{NAME_10}}: the building with floors above and below the ground

maths_rules: movement needed = target floor - starting floor = (-1) - (-2)
slip: floor -1 is above floor -2, so the lift goes up and the button is positive
video_script.design: The lift shaft is drawn below the ground only, two floors, one arrow going up.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the lift shaft below the ground, with the lift at floor -2 and floor -1 above it

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the lift shaft is drawn
marks.ask: floor -1 lights up and a button panel appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='start'/>The lift is at floor negative two, below the ground.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>It has to reach floor negative one. Which button should be pressed?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the shaft with floors -3, -2, -1, 0; the lift between floors; Starting floor + movement = Target floor

marks.below: the floors below the ground are shown with negative numbers
marks.order: an arrow shows floor -1 higher than floor -2
marks.rule: the line Starting floor + movement = Target floor is written

narration: <bookmark mark='below'/>Floors below the ground have negative numbers.
<bookmark mark='order'/>Floor negative one is higher than floor negative two, because it is nearer the ground.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>As before, the starting floor plus the movement gives the target floor.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the target floor is negative one, and the starting floor is negative two.

beats.on_screen: To find: the button press (movement needed)

marks.find: the words button press are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the button press, which is the movement needed.

beats.on_screen: Movement needed = target floor - starting floor

marks.rule: the rule target floor take away starting floor is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the movement needed is the target floor take away the starting floor.

marks.vals: the two floors are put in: (-1) - (-2)

narration: <bookmark mark='vals'/>Step two, put in the floors. We write negative one take away negative two.

beats.on_screen: (-2) + ? = (-1); an arrow from floor -2 up to floor -1

marks.arrow: an arrow rises from floor -2 to floor -1

narration: <bookmark mark='miss'/>Step three, read it on the shaft, negative two plus a missing movement equals negative one.
<bookmark mark='arrow'/>The lift must rise from floor negative two to floor negative one.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The button press is positive one.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check it, negative two plus positive one lands on negative one.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: -1 crossed out as the button; the shaft with an arrow going up from floor -2 to floor -1

marks.fix: the button is struck out and an upward arrow appears

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the button is negative one, because both floors have negative signs.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But floor negative one is above floor negative two, so the lift must go up.
<bookmark mark='signs'/>The signs on the floors do not decide the button, and the button is positive one.
